title: Rollout automation: add safeguard checks before expanding tiered batching rollout
author: Benji Okafor
description:
Context: runtime-1.22 introduces tiered batching defaults (fast/standard/cost-efficient). For the staged rollout (internal canary → hosted subset → dedicated opt-in → broader default), we need a single automated “expand rollout” step that refuses to proceed unless the safety signals are green.

This PR adds rollout automation hooks used by release tooling (release-bot + Console rollout workflow) and implements a set of safeguard checks:
- Perf gates: verifies perf-canary tier SLO gates are green for the target model family/hardware class/region set (fast p99 + standard p95) for the current release build.
- SLO / error-budget gates: checks fast-tier p99 burn-rate and request error-rate over a configurable window and blocks expansion on sustained burn.
- Dashboard sanity: ensures required tiered batching panels exist + are populated (latency histograms, queue depth, batch size distribution) for the target rollout scope.
- Kill-switch readiness: validates the rollout config includes a kill switch target and that the current config is retrievable (guards against “can’t roll back” class failures).
- Guardrail enforcement: blocks expansion when overload mode is engaged above threshold (load shedding activated or queue depth above cap for >N minutes).

Design notes:
- This is intentionally conservative: checks fail-closed for “unknown” unless explicitly configured as warn-only (used for early internal canaries).
- All checks emit structured reason codes and a short human summary used by release-bot comments + Console UI.
- All queries are scoped with cardinality controls (tier/model/region) to avoid reintroducing the tier-label blowup issues.

Operational flow:
- Release tooling calls: POST /internal/rollouts/{rollout_id}/expand with {from_stage, to_stage}.
- The runtime control-plane runs checks, returns either APPROVE or BLOCK with reason codes, and writes an audit event.
- If BLOCK, expansion stops; operator can either remediate or override with an explicit “break-glass” flag (RBAC-gated; logged).

Follow-ups (not in this PR):
- Add a “dry run” expansion view in Console (DES-771) showing which checks would block for the next stage.
- Add dedicated-specific checks for tenant override precedence drift (ENG-18430).

Rollout / risk:
- Feature-flagged behind rollout_safeguards_enabled (default ON for tiered batching rollouts, OFF for older rollouts until we backfill dashboards).
- Timeouts + fallback behavior designed to avoid wedging release tooling: each check has an upper bound and returns BLOCK on timeout (operators can override if needed).

Testing:
- Unit tests for each check type + reason code mapping.
- Integration test with fake metrics provider to cover windows, missing dashboards, and “stale data” blocking.
- Verified against staging with a synthetic rollout in us-east-1 and eu-west-1.

Refs:
- Perf canary gating PR: github/perf-canary#489
- Tiered dashboards PR: github/observability-pack#933

ci_checks:
Buildkite: redwood-runtime-unit ✅ | redwood-control-plane ✅ | gofmt/lint ✅ | integration-rollouts (staging) ✅ | security-sast ✅ | perf-smoke (non-gating) ⚪️

Notable: integration-rollouts failed once due to a too-tight 30s timeout when the fake provider injected jitter; increased to 90s and made the test deterministic.
conversation:
Rafael Mendes (SRE): “Fail-closed on timeout makes sense, but I’m worried about false blocks when the metrics backend is degraded. Do we have an operator-visible reason code vs a generic ‘unknown’?”
Benji Okafor (author): Added explicit reason codes per check (e.g., PERF_CANARY_TIMEOUT, METRICS_BACKEND_TIMEOUT, DASHBOARD_STALE_DATA) and included a link to the relevant dashboard/query in the summary.

Sean Gallagher (SRE): “Please gate on burn-rate (multi-window) rather than raw p99 spikes. We should avoid blocking on a single short-lived hiccup.”
Benji Okafor: Updated SLO gate to use 5m/30m windows with sustained-threshold logic (configurable). Added tests for transient spikes.

Allison Grant (Obs): “Dashboard ‘exists’ isn’t enough; we need to know it’s populated and not stale. Also please ensure we don’t query high-cardinality tags.”
Benji Okafor: Implemented data freshness check (must have samples within last 3 minutes) and hard-coded allowed label set (tier, model_family, region, hw_class). Added a guard that rejects queries containing request_id/route_id.

Marissa Cole (PM Rollouts): “Break-glass override needs to be explicit + audited. Can we also make warn-only configurable per stage?”
Benji Okafor: Added expand request option override=true (RBAC: release-operator). Writes audit event with actor + justification string. Added per-stage policy: {mode: block|warn}.

Connor O'Brien (Release Eng): “Release-bot needs a stable, machine-readable output. Please don’t rely on human text parsing.”
Benji Okafor: Response includes JSON enum status + list of reason codes + stable check ids; release-bot consumes that and formats text.

Requested changes addressed:
- Added explicit timeout reason codes + links
- Switched SLO gating to multi-window burn-rate
- Added staleness check for dashboards
- Added cardinality allowlist enforcement
- Added audited break-glass override
release_notes: Internal (runtime-1.22): Release tooling now gates tiered batching rollout expansion on perf-canary + SLO/error-budget + dashboard readiness checks. Operators can break-glass override with RBAC; all overrides are audited.
merge_outcome: Merged into release/runtime-1.22 via squash; deployed to staging rollout controller on 2026-04-10; release-bot config enabled for tiered-batching rollout IDs only.
